text: The two story files under 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P4 rwb-access (Access and authority)/ - RWB P4 AD012 APP Approve a rule version v1.md and RWB P4 AD012 CON Approve a rule version - contract v1.md - and the fragments _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P4-AD012-APP.json and RWB-P4-AD012-CON.json, all already present and written by the parallel Work Package B-P4-04 for the same two slices of legacy RWB-AD-012, stand as the deliverable of B2-P4-006: they are not rewritten, not versioned to v2 and not duplicated, and their missing values stay registered once as CG-B-P4-04-AD012-101 to -107 with ASM-B-P4-04-AD012-101 to -107. Their metadata, their 19 sections, AC1 and AC2 of RWB-AD-012 with their origin tags, the six new-under-D-RCV-60 criteria of the contract story, the six test case ids with the Level column, the nine section 12 tables and the five DP rows are kept unchanged, and B2-P4-006 registers only the duplicate-Work-Package finding.
why: The Work Package names the two story files and the two fragments as its outputs and all four already exist with complete content, because the plan issues two Work Packages for one legacy key (B-P4-04 inside a fanout and B2-P4-006 with fanout 0). Root AGENTS.md rule 1 forbids editing a file that already exists and forbids writing a path outside the Write only block, so the next-version copy that rule 1 would otherwise ask for cannot be created here, and rule 13 forbids stopping the run. The artefacts were therefore read, verified against Template and Rules v1 R7, R7.1, R7.2, R8.1 and R9 with the P4 context pack as the authority for service facts, and kept; the collision is recorded as one gap row and this row, in the same way as the parallel B2-P4-002 finding and the other B2 collisions of this run.
read: wp/B-P4-04.md and wp/B2-P4-006.md (the same four output paths); plan/split_plan.json (two slices for RWB-AD-012); gaps/B-P4-04.jsonl (7 rows cited by the four artefacts) and assumptions/B-P4-04.jsonl (7 rows); Template and Rules v1 R5.3, R5.4, R5.5, R5.7, R7, R7.1, R7.2, R8.1 and R9; context pack P4 (service row, ownership rows, naming rules); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md RWB-AD-012; FSD and TSD P4 v3
applied_in: whole file set of RWB-AD-012 in RWB-SVC-P4; fragments RWB-P4-AD012-APP.json and RWB-P4-AD012-CON.json
confirm: Delivery lead with the coordinating agent of stage B2 when the plan is regenerated with one Work Package per legacy key
impact: If B2-P4-006 is retired for this key, nothing changes in the tree; if a B2 citation family is required instead, only the CG and ASM ids in the two story files and in the two fragments change, and no wording, table, field or test case.

text: The contract slice RWB-P4-AD012-CON owns no legacy acceptance criterion, because acs is empty on its line in the plan and in the Work Package, so its section 16 carries its own contract test ids TC-AD-012-CON-01 to TC-AD-012-CON-06 at Level Contract, and the four legacy ids TC-AD-012-01 to TC-AD-012-04 stay with the app slice RWB-P4-AD012-APP, where they test AC1, AC2, AC6 and AC5. The tcs_legacy list on the contract line is therefore satisfied by ownership and not by a second copy of the four rows.
why: WP item 5 keeps the legacy test case ids of the acceptance criteria a story owns and deviates only for an integration copy; the contract story owns none of the two legacy criteria, so restating the four ids in its own section 16 would give one test case two owners and two Covers values.
